name: Adult Hepatocellular Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Characteristic arterial phase hyperenhancement with washout in venous or delayed phases on contrast-enhanced imaging (CT or MRI)
Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels above 400 ng/mL
Histological confirmation of malignant hepatocellular tumor cells by biopsy
Underlying chronic liver disease or cirrhosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical imaging features on contrast-enhanced CT or MRI with or without elevated AFP; biopsy if imaging and AFP are inconclusive
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Biopsy is reserved for atypical imaging or when non-invasive criteria are not met

pathognomonic.notes: Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera due to bile duct obstruction or liver failure

common.notes: Dull or sharp pain localized to liver area
Abdominal fluid accumulation secondary to portal hypertension or liver failure

occasional.notes: Low-grade fever due to tumor necrosis or inflammation
Confusion or altered mental status due to liver failure
Hormonal imbalance due to liver dysfunction
Vascular lesions associated with liver disease

rare.notes: Due to ectopic production of parathyroid hormone-related protein
Increased red blood cell mass from ectopic erythropoietin production
Elevated platelet count as a paraneoplastic phenomenon

laboratory: Abnormal liver function tests (elevated ALT, AST, bilirubin)
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing arterial phase hyperenhancement and venous washout
Ultrasound with Doppler showing hepatic mass with increased vascularity
other: Underlying cirrhosis or chronic hepatitis B/C infection
Portal vein thrombosis in advanced cases

distinguishingFeatures: Bile duct origin with delayed contrast enhancement
Multiple liver lesions rather than solitary mass

redFlags: Severe abdominal pain with signs of hemorrhage
references: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases Practice Guidelines, 2018
European Association for the Study of the Liver Clinical Practice Guidelines, 2018
UpToDate: Hepatocellular carcinoma: Epidemiology, etiology, and screening
